Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a left-sided pleural effusion with an irregular, nodular opacity in the left lower lung zone/pleura, which is highly suggestive of an underlying malignancy such as lung cancer rather than the smooth meniscus of heart failure or the consolidation of pneumonia. In a 73-year-old patient, this radiographic appearance combined with a unilateral effusion makes malignant pleural effusion the most likely diagnosis among the choices.
